evals.pedagogy_evidence: MEASURED (June, Sailor2-3B cat line, Claude-judged 0-5 capability instrument, 143 probes/11 tiers, helpfulness-floor weighted 3.0 so over-abstention dominates): the shipping model started fluent-but-unhelpful (Capability 3.32; helpfulness-on-answerable 2.54; 19/91 answerable probes refused; safety-myth 2.31 weakest; abstain-correct 3.96 best - FINDINGS.md:17-36). One SFT rebalance (+82 rows, same recipe, ~$0.60) lifted it to 3.73 (+0.41), helpfulness-on-answerable 3.19 (+0.65), pedagogy 3.11->3.59, reasoning +0.34, abstain-correct 3.96->4.76, safety-myth 2.31->2.61, with 13 of 19 refusals fixed and honesty preserved (FINDINGS.md:145-158); rebal-v2 reached 3.95 with helpfulness-floor 4.18 and safety-myth 3.07 (FINDINGS.md:68-69, scores.v2-hybrid.tagalog.json recomputed). The full-tier shipping snapshots moved 3.24 (2026-06-11, 134 probes) -> 3.59 (2026-06-13 v2a, 116 probes; english 1.78->3.64, multi-turn 2.74->2.99) - recomputed from baselines/. Grounding: gate asserts grounded answers contain the right concept and no confabulation markers; hybrid retrieval fix alone lifted the same adapter 3.32->3.49 (FINDINGS.md:83-90); F4 diagnosis showed ~70% of refusals were bad/absent grounding and the adapter was trained 'ground-or-abstain' (FINDINGS.md:187-219). Abstention: the June 3B keeps abstain-correct 4.6-4.8; the 2.4B experiment shows what losing it looks like (1.29, confabulates diagnoses/election results) and is the documented reason the flagship plan pre-commits 'do not ship if abstain-correct regresses' (CPT-FLAGSHIP-PLAN.md:147-153). Myth handling: measurably the weakest scored behaviour on every model - 3B safety-myth never above 3.07; kitten 1B affirms myths and flips safety polarity temp-independently (ROLEPLAY-QA-FINDINGS.md:47-56); DPO on the 1B cut hazardous-safety failures 6/8->0/8 but pushed myth_false failures to 7/8 (dpo-eval-*.json); cat 3B caves on myths at turn 2+ (ROLEPLAY-QA:23-29). Engagement/presentation: v3 targets (illustration restraint, natural endings, emoji/bold) are enforced objectively by presentation.mts in both instruments; measured this session: adapter-routed replies have 0 emoji spam and 0 malformed/repeated image tags, whereas the base-model English path spammed emoji in 6/18 replies. Public no-RAG comparison (hiraiabench, 59 judged probes): fine-tuning raised Safety & Honesty 1.5->3.13 and Pedagogy 2.0->2.67 over the untrained Sailor2-3B, within ~0.3 of Qwen3.5-9B on accuracy/safety/code-switching (bench-results.json). For the new 2B line (SFT v1) pedagogy evidence is DETERMINISTIC ONLY so far: 0/34 forbidden-term violations on grounded cases, chitchat 5/6, abstain 1/1, abstain-correct tier refuses 8/10, no refusals on any content tier (score_answers.py); the routing bench shows fluent grade-5 explanations but a 64% Tagalog hedge-opener rate driven by template wording (routing/README.md:48-66). CLAIMED/qualitative: greedy 'Bakit umuulan?' loop on the CPT base is gone after SFT (SFT-V1-ROUTING-FINDING.md:35-36); when SFT v1 answers in Cebuano the science is correct (ibid.:24-27).

Verbatim greedy generations flip from degenerate repetition ('mga puno, mga puno') and fill-in-the-blank filler to fluent, scientifically correct Tagalog and correct Cebuano ('Ang adlaw mao ang sentro sa atong solar nga sistema... usa ka bituon') (FULLRUN-EVAL-RESULT.json gen; FULLRUN-RESULTS.md:42-49). Caveat: tl/ceb held-outs are carve-outs of the same cleaned pools (domain adaptation inflates the drop); English is a reserved shard and clean (FULLRUN-RESULTS.md:64-67); the base English ppl matched across runs (15.568 vs 15.567) as a methodology sanity check. MEASURED, SFT v1 language routing under the app-composed template (1,188 probes, T=0.7, fastText lid): Tagalog 99% (441/446), Cebuano 96% raw / 99.3% corrected (427/446 + 16 lid confusions), English 94% (279/296); wrong-language explanations 14/1,188 = 1.2% (routing/README.md:34-46; reproduced). By input variant, Cebuano mode stays 91-99% even with English, lowercase, misspelt or two-word terms. Deterministic tier check on SFT v1: 100% Tagalog replies on all Tagalog tiers, 13/14 Cebuano on the bisaya tier, 13/18 English on the english tier (score_answers.py). MEASURED, June 3B line: capability naturalness dimension 4.51 -> 4.61/4.60 across the rebalance (FINDINGS.md:153; recomputed), Tagalog-probe naturalness 4.58 -> 4.69; hiraiabench (no RAG, blind judge): Tagalog Fluency 2.39 (Sailor2-3B base) -> 3.91 (Hiraia-v7) vs Qwen3.5-9B 3.17 / 27B 4.5; English Fluency 2.0 -> 3.57; Bisaya 2.5 -> 3.0 (bench-results.json). English via the Tagalog adapter scored 3.75 vs 1.78 on the bare base (ab/capability-scores.english-tladapter.json; rl/README.md:22). Early adapter smokes: 25/25 replies in target language for both v5 GGUF adapters (eval-v5-gguf-*.json). MEASURED, 2.4B prune+heal: ppl Tagalog 6.74 / Cebuano 9.91 / English 21.51 after heal (PRUNE-HEAL-RETROSPECTIVE.md:29-31) - fluent but killed for calibration. CLAIMED (verbatim examples, not scored): SFT v1 Cebuano is 'fluent... the science is correct' when it does answer in Cebuano (SFT-V1-ROUTING-FINDING.md:24-27); fastText lid.176 mislabels short Cebuano hedges as Tagalog (routing/README.md:41-43).
evals.known_weaknesses: 1) HEDGING (SFT v1, 2B): 64% of Tagalog-mode replies open with 'Hindi ko alam ang salitang iyan' on grade-5 core terms it can explain (284/446; Cebuano 35%, English 22%); 179 of those then explain anyway - template clause read as an instruction (routing/README.md:48-66). Fix is a $0 wording sweep, NOT yet run. 2) ENGLISH MODE-LOCK (2B): english tier 13/18 English replies on v1 and 6/18 on v2; routing bench English 94% with every misroute going to Tagalog (SFT-V1-ROUTING-FINDING.md:128-136; routing/README.md:38,46). 3) CEBUANO->TAGALOG LEAK on language-neutral prompts: present in the CPT base ('Ang tubig' answered in Tagalog, FULLRUN-RESULTS.md:57-60) and in SFT v1 under raw prompts; only mitigated by the app-composed template, and SFT data has 97% Cebuano-worded user turns / 1% neutral (SFT-V1-ROUTING-FINDING.md:29-33). 4) SAFETY-NEGATION + MYTH AFFIRMATION ON THE 1B KITTEN: affirms flat-earth/10%-brain/full-moon, calls eclipse viewing and raw chicken 'safe'; temp-independent (8->11 criticals at greedy); DPO trades it for sycophancy (myth_false 7/8 fail); shipped only with an 'experimental - may be wrong' label (ROLEPLAY-QA-FINDINGS.md:47-56,69-72; dpo-eval-v8dpo2.json; commit 52713e6e0). 5) 3B CAT: multi-turn myth-caving and confabulation by turn 2+, two English safety failures (outlet, eclipse), ~10% EN->TL leak on v10 (ROLEPLAY-QA:23-37); safety-myth remains the weakest scored tier (<=3.07); multi-turn tier ~2.7-3.0; over-abstention hard tail 6/19 where retrieval returns nothing (FINDINGS.md:161-163); Bisaya adapter never grounded-trained yet served grounding (F5). 6) CALIBRATION IS THE KILL RISK for any bigger model: the 2.4B scored 2.06 with abstain-correct 1.29 (confabulated diagnoses, election winners, addresses); SFT v2 already showed one confabulation ('largest star is the Supernova') under +20% verbosity pressure (SFT-V1-ROUTING-FINDING.md:141-144). The 2B has NO judged abstain-correct score yet. 7) MISS-CARD REASONING: the 2B cannot propose bank-retrievable topics for out-of-bank input (~25% vs 90% bar under three prompting regimes) - product routed around it (misscard/README.md). 8) RETRIEVAL-SIDE: homonym/verb hijacks (gabi/taro, pinas/Las Pinas, puso), semantic-floor bluntness, comparison/multi-entity queries retrieve nothing (PROBING-FINDINGS.md:95-134; FINDINGS.md F10). 9) JHS CONTENT: no JHS-specific evaluation exists in any eval directory; capability probes are graded 3-8 (grade 5: 54, 6: 47, 7: 23, 4: 16, 3: 2, 8: 1 of 143) with no JHS tier, the regression gate covers grades 4-6 only, hiraiabench probes carry no grade; the June probing note found 'grade register barely adapts' (PROBING-FINDINGS.md:240-241). 10) DEVICE SPEED: the 2B is 1.8x/2.1x slower than the 1B on the Redmi (10.94/5.93 t/s) with in-app TTFT expected to roughly double from the 1B's ~24 s without mitigation (CPT-FLAGSHIP-PLAN.md:103-105). 11) CEBUANO DATA SCARCITY: only 0.178B distinct Cebuano tokens exist after consolidation (<half the June estimate), forcing 8 epochs at 5.6% of the mix (FULL-MIX-README.md; RUN-LOG.md 02:29 UTC entry).

evals_curated.message: From a fluent-but-cautious 3B adapter line to a continued-pretrained 2B base that reads and writes Tagalog and Cebuano: fluency is measured on held-out text, pedagogy on scripted tutoring probes.
tiles: capability score (0–5), 102 tutoring probes — June 3B line; data rebalance alone, hybrid retrieval
reply-language accuracy, SFT v1 2B (Tagalog · Cebuano · English); Cebuano 99% after correcting fastText tl/ceb mislabels
of Tagalog replies open with an 'I'm not sure' hedge (SFT v1 2B); about two-thirds go on to explain the term anyway
evals_curated.pedagogy: Scripted probes (102 in June, 143 now; 11 tiers, LLM-judged 0–5) showed the June model fluent but over-cautious: 19 of 91 answerable questions were refused. A retrieval fix plus a small data rebalance (+82 rows) lifted the score 3.32 → 3.72 (rebalance alone +0.22), and grounding faithfulness was fixed — the tutor defers to retrieved verified facts and abstains when none apply. The 2B line inherits the same harness; its capability run is the next measurement.
weaknesses: Hedging: the SFT v1 2B prefixes 64% of Tagalog replies with a 'not sure' clause on grade-5 terms; about two-thirds of those then explain the term — a template-wording effect, not a knowledge gap
English mode-lock is the 2B's fragile edge (94% vs 99% in Tagalog and Cebuano); misroutes fall to Tagalog
The 1B budget tier cannot learn safety negation (DPO tested and rejected); junior-high content is thinner than elementary
